content.title: ESC 2023 Recommendations — ACS with Cardiogenic Shock (excerpt)

recommendations.recommendation: Immediate coronary angiography and PCI of the IRA (if indicated) is recommended in patients with CS complicating ACS.
recommendations.notes: First-line reperfusion strategy for ACS with cardiogenic shock; PCI of infarct-related artery (IRA).

recommendations.recommendation: Emergency CABG is recommended for ACS-related CS if PCI of the IRA is not feasible/unsuccessful.
recommendations.notes: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) as alternative when PCI not possible or fails.

recommendations.recommendation: In cases of haemodynamic instability, emergency surgical/catheter-based repair of mechanical complications of ACS is recommended, based on Heart Team discussion.
recommendations.notes: Repair of mechanical complications (surgical or catheter-based) guided by Heart Team.

recommendations.recommendation: Fibrinolysis should be considered in STEMI patients presenting with CS if a PPCI strategy is not available within 120 min from the time of STEMI diagnosis and mechanical complications have been ruled out.
recommendations.notes: Consider fibrinolysis when timely primary PCI (PPCI) cannot be delivered; ensure no mechanical complications.

recommendations.recommendation: In patients with ACS and severe/refractory CS, short-term mechanical circulatory support may be considered.
recommendations.notes: Consider short-term MCS for severe or refractory cardiogenic shock.

recommendations.recommendation: The routine use of an IABP in ACS patients with CS and without mechanical complications is not recommended.
recommendations.notes: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) not routinely recommended in ACS with CS absent mechanical complications.
